newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-STEWART STROKES UNBEATEN DOUBLE CENTURY.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-STEWART STROKES UNBEATEN DOUBLE CENTURY.

text.p: England wicketkeeper-batsman Alec Stewart stroked a superb unbeaten double century as Surrey flayed Yorkshire's attack in their county championship match on Thursday.
Stewart was at his belligerent best, hitting 30 fours and a six in making exactly 200 not out as Surrey piled up 426 for six at the close on the first day of the four-day game at The Oval.

Brothers Ben and Adam Hollioake figured in century stands with Stewart, who scored his runs from 236 balls and is on the brink of beating his highest first-class innings of 206 not out against Essex in 1989.
Stewart added 141 in two hours for the third wicket with Ben Hollioake (53) and 132 in 142 balls for the fifth wicket with captain Adam Hollioake, who struck 69 off 72 deliveries.

Stewart's test team mate, off-spinner Robert Croft, hit his highest score for two years with 82 to help Glamorgan recover from a bad start to make 272 for nine at the close against Middlesex at Cardiff.
Croft came to the crease with Glamorgan rocking at 64 for four and when he was eighth out his team had moved on to a healthier 240.

The slow bowler reached his second half-century of the season off 119 balls, with seven boundaries, and had added two more fours before he was caught behind, trying to hook a lifter from paceman Angus Fraser.
Worcestershire's stand-in captain Steve Rhodes led a fightback against leaders Gloucestershire at Bristol, after his decision to bat first in poor morning light initially backfired.

The visitors slumped to 65 for six by the first over after lunch but then Rhodes, leading the side in place of unwell Australian Tom Moody, made a painstaking 78 before being bowled by the final ball of the day with his side on 243 for eight.
Vince Clarke agonisingly missed a maiden century, after leading Derbyshire to a fragile 200 against Warwickshire at Edgbaston.
The 25-year-old Anglo-Australian went in at 16 for four and was last out for 99 when he was caught at the wicket, attempting to cut left-arm spinner Ashley Giles.

His battling performance lasted for three hours and brought 14 boundaries from 159 balls as he revived a side rocked by the resignation earlier in the day of captain Dean Jones, the former Australian test batsman.
